llm.summary: This skill is transparent about building and installing other skills, but its update and uninstall flows have safety gaps that could persist unsafe instructions or delete the wrong files.

dimensions.detail: Telegram integration is purpose-aligned, but default discovery loads several generic OpenClaw .env files and imports every key into the process environment, exposing unrelated secrets to later code and subprocesses.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Install is plan-only by default and signed approval is documented, but the approved uninstall flow reads the actual deletion target from a mutable manifest rather than the approved target path, allowing an attacker with manifest write access to redirect deletion within the process user's filesystem permissions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The evolution flow copies feedback-derived text into a linked reference file and adds feedback-derived trigger cues to SKILL.md. Feedback is redacted for secrets, but instruction-like text, Markdown structure, and role/tool directives are not neutralized before becoming agent-loaded skill material.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can install generated skills and a macOS LaunchAgent for nightly review. The persistence is disclosed and has plan/uninstall paths, but it compounds the risk of the feedback-to-instructions issue if evolved candidates are approved without careful review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent with the package: it detects recurring needs, scaffolds candidate skills, validates them, records feedback, proposes updates, and can install or uninstall skills with Telegram approval. These are high-impact agent-behavior mutation capabilities, so the implementation details matter.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this only in a controlled workspace until the update and uninstall flows are fixed. Prefer plan-only mode, review generated and evolved skill folders before approval, use a dedicated Telegram env file containing only Telegram values, avoid generic .env auto-discovery, and do not enable scheduled or Telegram-approved mutations unless you trust the local install manifest and feedback source.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The Telegram bot token is used in requests to the official Telegram Bot API for approval and reporting. I did not find evidence that unrelated environment variables are intentionally sent to arbitrary network destinations, so this is expected integration behavior rather than confirmed credential exfiltration.
[TP4] expected: The lower-level install and Telegram wrapper scripts are explicitly listed in SKILL.md and are compatibility wrappers around documented scripts. I did not treat the wrapper pattern itself as hidden tool poisoning.
[T01] unexpected: The finding is supported: propose_skill_update.py writes raw feedback fields into references/evolution-feedback.md and links that file from SKILL.md, while validation focuses on structure and does not neutralize instruction injection.
[T09] unexpected: The uninstall finding is supported: approval checks target_root/skill_name, but uninstall_skill() later deletes record['target'] from .skill-forge-installs.json without containment or equality checks against the approved path.
[T09] unexpected: The environment-loading finding is supported: telegram_config.py loads multiple generic env files and copies all keys into os.environ even though the Telegram workflow only needs bot token and chat ID.
